::: {#exr-miller-taylor-cos-scaled}
#### Taylor expansion of a scaled cosine

Adapted from @problifesavercalc, Question 1.1.18.

Find the terms up to degree 4 in the Taylor series for

$$f(x) = \cos(5x)$$

at $x_0 = 0$.
:::

::: {#sol-miller-taylor-cos-scaled}
Recall the standard Maclaurin series for cosine:

$$\cos u = 1 - \frac{u^2}{2!} + \frac{u^4}{4!} - \dots$$

Substitute $u = 5x$:

$$\cos(5x) = 1 - \frac{(5x)^2}{2!} + \frac{(5x)^4}{4!} - \dots = 1 - \frac{25}{2}x^2 + \frac{625}{24}x^4 - \dots$$

*Remark:* Substituting into known Taylor expansions avoids computing high-order derivatives by hand.
:::
